title: Onramp bridge handoff - 7day skill fingerprint
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic 7-day onramp + mentor-shadow handoff used for generalist engineering hires (infra / platform / serving-runtime rotations). The aim is to rapidly produce an initial skills fingerprint, unblock the new hire for independent work, and capture interview-to-onboard alignment signals for later calibration.

Audience:
- Hiring manager (HM)
- Mentor (M)
- People Ops coordinator (PO)
- Candidate / new hire (NH)

High level goals:
- Day 7: NH can run local dev stack, open a small PR, and present a 15-min micro-project result.
- Produce a 1-page "skill fingerprint" that maps interview signals to day-7 outcomes.
- Capture open risks and remediation plan for first 30 days.

Hiring plan (pre-start checklist):
- Confirm role expectations with HM: top-3 deliverables first 90 days (short bullets).
- Assign mentor and secondary buddy (name + calendar invite).
- Provision accounts: laptop image, Okta groups, cloud IAM, internal wiki access.
- Create repo fork + starter issue (#0-setup) before day 1.
- Prep micro-project template in repo (see Micro-project section).

Interview rubric — quick reference (used to produce hire evidence):
Scoring: 1–4 (1 = not demonstrated, 4 = exceeds expectations)
- Technical fundamentals (TF): data structures, debugging, shell competence.
- System comprehension (SC): reading code, tracing request/response, explaining tradeoffs.
- Ownership & clarity (OC): communication, doc-writing, follow-ups.
- Collaboration (COL): pair-programming, feedback, cross-team empathy.
- Production readiness (PR): safety, monitoring, rollback thoughtfulness.

Anchors/examples:
- TF: 3 = quickly finds bug in unit test, explains fix; 2 = needs hints; 4 = finds broader pattern and writes small test.
- SC: 3 = can sketch request path through codebase; 4 = suggests targeted instrumentation.

Calibration notes for interviewers (short):
- Prefer evidence over impression: point to specific commits/comments from the takehome or pairing session.
- If unsure between 2/3, prioritize signalling around debugging velocity (ability to triage).

Micro-project (day 1 assigned, due day 6):
- Goal: add an end-to-end feature toggle + smoke test for an existing small endpoint (example repo: onboarding-starter).
- Acceptance: CI passes, one unit test added, README update with how to enable toggle locally, and a PR with clear description and context.
- Constraints: keep change < 120 lines, avoid infra churn, stub external downstreams.

7-day onramp schedule (detailed):
Day 0 (pre-boarding) — PO
- laptop + image ready, access sent, welcome mail with schedule and links.
Day 1 — Orientation + quick setup (HM + M)
- 9:00 intro with HM (expectations, deliverables).
- 10:00 mentor sync: repo tour, run local stack (pair).
- Afternoon: claim micro-project, create branch, push scaffold.
Day 2 — Deep shadow + small task (M)
- Morning: shadow mentor on one incident or triage (watch + note).
- Afternoon: implement first small change from micro-project; open WIP PR.
Day 3 — Pair & feedback loop (M + peer)
- Pair on a codepath adjacent to micro-project for 90 mins.
- End of day: 30-min feedback sync (mentor -> NH) capturing 3 strengths and 2 growth areas.
Day 4 — Independent work + docs (NH)
- Finish feature, update README, add test, run CI.
- Submit PR and request reviewers (mentor + one peer).
Day 5 — Review & deploy staging (HM)
- Address review comments; run staging smoke.
- Prepare 15-min demo slides (what, why, how).
Day 6 — Demo + skill fingerprint (NH + M + HM)
- 15-min demo + 10-min Q&A.
- HM + M complete day-7 checklist and fill skill fingerprint template.
Day 7 — 1:1 + plan (HM)
- 30-min 1:1: agree on first-30-day plan; sync on blockers; finalize onboarding notes.

Day-7 deliverables (artifacts):
- PR link + CI status
- README change + local run instructions
- 15-min demo notes / slides
- Skill fingerprint (single paragraph per rubric category + numeric scores)
- Risk log (0–3 bullets) and remediation plan

Skill fingerprint template (fillable fields shown inline):
- TF: "score - evidence"
- SC: "score - evidence"
- OC: "score - evidence"
- COL: "score - evidence"
- PR: "score - evidence"
- Overall recommendation: "green / yellow / red" + short rationale

Access checklist (The usual friction sources):
- Okta groups: dev, staging, infra-admin (if applicable)
- GitHub: org invite, repo permissions (write), PAT instruction
- Cloud: dev-project reader + deployer where needed
- Slack: #team, #oncall-rotations, #buddy-channel
- Monitoring: pager access read, dashboards link

Mentor playbook (short):
- Day 1 pair > 3 x 45min sprints over first 3 days.
- Give incremental tasks, keep feedback specific (example: "explain request flow in 5 bullets").
- Flag risks early: if PR not opened by day 3, escalate to HM and PO.

Communication templates (copy/paste friendly):
- Pre-boarding email subject: "Welcome to Redwood — day 1 plan + access"
- 1:1 opener: "Quick check: how did setup go? What's blocking you? One win since last sync?"

Risk flags + remediation (quick):
- No PR by Day 4 -> escalate, schedule 60-min pairing and re-scope micro-project.
- Persistent test flakiness -> mentor helps reproduce locally, HM may reassign test ownership.
- Security concerns (e.g., secret in PR) -> immediate rollback + security oncall notified.

Evaluation & follow-ups:
- HM to fill the fingerprint + recommendation within 48h of day 6 demo.
- PO to run 30-day pulse survey and collect mentor notes at day 14 and day 30.

Notes to self (things we still iterate on):
- Shorten micro-project to 3 small tasks if hiring for heavy infra roles; keep full feature for product-adjacent hires.
- Consider a lightweight rubric variant for senior ICs (prioritize system-level reasoning & leadership).
- Add short video walkthrough template for mentor pair sessions to improve asynchronous knowledge transfer.

Open questions (to discuss in People Ops sync):
- Should we standardize an "onramp difficulty" slider per role (green/yellow/red) visible on offer?
- How to better capture "learning velocity" metric during first 7 days?

---
End of doc. This is intentionally lean and tactical — meant to be copyable into an offer/onboarding packet and editable per team.
short_summary: Compact 7-day onramp + mentor-shadow playbook for engineering hires with interview rubric, micro-project and day-by-day checklist.
